findings.issue_text: [High/concurrency] dualwriter_mode3.go (Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection): Legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines with a 10s timeout and no retry, error logging, or surfacing; failed/timeout legacy writes are silently dropped (only a metric recorded), causing permanent divergence between LegacyStorage and Storage during dual-write migration.

[High/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Update: The legacy goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update with the original objInfo, dropping the updateWrapper that previously pinned the object to what Storage wrote; Legacy calls objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own old object, producing a different result (or a create instead of update) and divergent data.

[High/concurrency] dualwriter_mode3.go (Create/Delete/DeleteCollection): The same runtime.Object/request ctx is passed to the async legacy goroutine while the caller continues using it, risking races on shared state; deriving the timeout from the request context means a client disconnect after the response cancels the legacy write.

[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Create: On storage-create error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, recording the storage failure as a legacy metric; same mistake in Update's error path.

[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:DeleteCollection: The async legacy goroutine records d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy delete-collection failures are recorded under storage metrics and legacy latency is never tracked.

[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Delete: ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) replaces the enriched log (with name/kind/method values) with the base logger, so the Delete error log loses request-specific fields that all other methods attach.

[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Delete: Success path records d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...) passing name where every other call passes options.Kind as the kind label, producing inconsistent metric label cardinality.

[Low/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Create: The async legacy Create result (including failure) is never logged, so operators get no signal besides a counter; on success the function returns err which is guaranteed nil only by inspection.

[Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go: Tests use an undefined identifier p in TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_List, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_DeleteCollection, and TestMode3_Update (no prometheus.NewRegistry() call, unlike TestMode3_Get), which will fail to compile; looks like an incomplete edit.

[Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go: Because legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines, tests set legacy mocks that are never invoked and success-case tests never assert the legacy call happened (no m.AssertExpectations/mock count check); tests neither verify legacy mirroring nor are deterministic for async paths — they can pass even if legacy writes are completely broken.

[Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go: TestMode3_Update never tests the case where legacy Update fails while storage succeeds, and no test covers the legacy timeout/cancellation behavior of the new 10s async writes.

[Low/data] dualwriter_mode3.go:Create: Storage Create succeeds and returns, but the legacy Create goroutine may execute after the response; if the process crashes or the write times out, the object exists only in Storage — Mode 3 write-both semantics are now only best-effort with no reconciliation, which the PR description should make explicit.

[Low/doc_defect] dualwriter_mode3.go: Mode comments still say "writes to LegacyStorage and Storage", but behavior changed from synchronous dual-write to async best-effort mirroring; the doc comments are misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/concurrency] dualwriter_mode3.go (Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection): Legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines with a 10s timeout and no retry, error logging, or surfacing; failed/timeout legacy writes are silently dropped (only a metric recorded), causing permanent divergence between LegacyStorage and Storage during dual-write migration.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection now perform the LegacyStorage operation in a detached goroutine with context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, ...) and do not log or return any error from the legacy write (e.g., Create: legacy write happens in go func() and its err is only used to call d.recordLegacyDuration; similarly for Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). This is a concrete behavior change from the prior synchronous legacy call that at least logged errors, and it can indeed allow silent legacy-write failures/timeouts without any retry/surfacing, which is a migration/consistency concern rather than a directly verifiable correctness defect given the diff doesn’t state required dual-write guarantees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Update: The legacy goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update with the original objInfo, dropping the updateWrapper that previously pinned the object to what Storage wrote; Legacy calls objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own old object, producing a different result (or a create instead of update) and divergent data.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Update(), the previous implementation computed `updated := objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)`, wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper{updated: updated}`, and ensured Legacy.Update used the same object that Storage wrote. The new implementation calls `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` with the original `objInfo` (no wrapper / pinning to `res`). This allows Legacy.Update to re-run `UpdatedObject` against Legacy’s own existing object (or perform a create path), which can produce a different result than Storage wrote, causing divergence—matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/concurrency] dualwriter_mode3.go (Create/Delete/DeleteCollection): The same runtime.Object/request ctx is passed to the async legacy goroutine while the caller continues using it, risking races on shared state; deriving the timeout from the request context means a client disconnect after the response cancels the legacy write.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Delete/DeleteCollection launch async legacy writes using the same request-scoped ctx: e.g. `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...); ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) }()`. Since this ctx is derived from the incoming request context, it will be canceled when the request finishes/client disconnects, which can prematurely abort the legacy write and leave legacy storage out of sync. The finding’s race concern is also diff-grounded: the goroutine reuses the same `runtime.Object` (`obj`) and ctx while the caller continues, which risks concurrent access if either side mutates shared state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Create: On storage-create error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, recording the storage failure as a legacy metric; same mistake in Update's error path.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, the error path after `d.Storage.Create(...)` fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` even though the timed operation (`startStorage := time.Now()`) is the storage create. This misattributes a storage failure/duration to legacy metrics. The same misattribution exists in DualWriterMode3.Update: on `d.Storage.Update(...)` error it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` instead of recording a storage metric.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:DeleteCollection: The async legacy goroutine records d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy delete-collection failures are recorded under storage metrics and legacy latency is never tracked.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection starts an async goroutine to call d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...), but then records the duration via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ... startLegacy) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. This misattributes legacy delete-collection latency/failures to storage metrics and prevents legacy metrics from being tracked for that path, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go:Create: The async legacy Create result (including failure) is never logged, so operators get no signal besides a counter; on success the function returns err which is guaranteed nil only by inspection.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the legacy write is executed in a goroutine and the returned error is only fed into `d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)` with no `log.Error(...)` or other log/trace of failure/success (`go func() { ... _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(...) }()`). That matches the finding: operators would only have metrics/counters for async legacy failures. The note about returning `err` being nil “only by inspection” is true but not a correctness defect, since `err` is the `Storage.Create` error and is nil on the success path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go: Tests use an undefined identifier p in TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_List, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_DeleteCollection, and TestMode3_Update (no prometheus.NewRegistry() call, unlike TestMode3_Get), which will fail to compile; looks like an incomplete edit.

adjudication.rationale: Within dualwriter_mode3_test.go the identifier `p` is not defined in the shown function scopes, but Go tests compile at the package level across files. The diff also removes a local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` in dualwriter_mode1_test.go while still passing `p` to `NewDualWriter`, strongly suggesting `p` is defined at package scope elsewhere (not shown in this diff). Therefore it’s not verifiable from the diff that `p` is undefined / that the tests won’t compile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go: Because legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines, tests set legacy mocks that are never invoked and success-case tests never assert the legacy call happened (no m.AssertExpectations/mock count check); tests neither verify legacy mirroring nor are deterministic for async paths — they can pass even if legacy writes are completely broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy operations for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection are executed in `go func(){... d.Legacy.<op>(...) ...}()` fire-and-forget goroutines with a timeout. In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, success-path tests often set up legacy mock expectations (e.g., `TestMode3_Create` and `TestMode3_Update`) but never assert they were met (no `m.AssertExpectations(t)` / call counts), and they do not wait for the async goroutine to run. This makes the tests non-deterministic for async paths and allows them to pass even if the legacy mirroring never happens (unused expectations are not checked).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go: TestMode3_Update never tests the case where legacy Update fails while storage succeeds, and no test covers the legacy timeout/cancellation behavior of the new 10s async writes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new async legacy writes with 10s timeouts in Mode3 (e.g., Update/Create/Delete/DeleteCollection now spawn `go func()` and use `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., time.Second*10, ...)`). In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `TestMode3_Update` only covers (a) storage success + legacy success (both mocks return nil error) and (b) storage failure; it does not cover the case where `Storage.Update` succeeds but `Legacy.Update` fails, nor does any test exercise the new timeout/cancellation behavior of the async legacy goroutines. This is a concrete test gap for newly introduced nontrivial behavior, but not a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] dualwriter_mode3.go:Create: Storage Create succeeds and returns, but the legacy Create goroutine may execute after the response; if the process crashes or the write times out, the object exists only in Storage — Mode 3 write-both semantics are now only best-effort with no reconciliation, which the PR description should make explicit.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection now perform the LegacyStorage operation in a fire-and-forget goroutine with a 10s timeout (e.g., Create: after Storage.Create succeeds, it immediately returns and launches go func() { d.Legacy.Create(...) }). Any legacy error/timeout is not surfaced to the caller, and a crash after returning can leave the object written only to Storage, contradicting the file’s stated Mode 3 semantics (“writing to LegacyStorage and Storage”). This is a real behavioral/correctness change that can cause persistent divergence/data loss on the legacy side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] dualwriter_mode3.go: Mode comments still say "writes to LegacyStorage and Storage", but behavior changed from synchronous dual-write to async best-effort mirroring; the doc comments are misleading.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the Mode3 doc comments still describe dual-write behavior in a generic/synchronous sense (e.g., "Mode 3 represents writing to LegacyStorage and Storage" and method comments like "writes to LegacyStorage and Storage"), but the implementation now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines with timeouts (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). This makes the comments potentially misleading about guarantees (best-effort mirroring vs required/synchronous).
